artifacts.summary: Characterizes the deploy_pending vs identical-dispatch guard composition defect: reconcile-task-status.sh runs only once at /orchestrate entry, never after the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint's mid-run deploy, so a deploy-unblocked task can only converge via a re-derived identical dispatch that trips the guard. Recommends wiring an automatic reconcile pass into the checkpoint's clean-success path as the primary fix, plus a streak-freeze (not full suppression) backstop on the guard, and correcting the 'no manual action needed' message.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's /orchestrate engine, reconcile-task-status.sh is invoked exactly once per invocation (at entry, before Move 1's first cycle) -- never per-cycle inside the loop. Any mid-run event that unblocks a stuck task's status (e.g. the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint's deploy landing) has no in-loop mechanism to re-run reconcile and pick up the unblock within the same run; only a fresh dispatch re-derivation or a subsequent /orchestrate invocation's entry-reconcile will. When designing a mid-run self-healing hook, the checkpoint boundary (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, strictly before Move 2 issues dispatches, the one point with no dispatch in flight) is the safe serialized insertion point, matching the existing Concurrency Posture rationale for why the redeploy trigger itself lives only there.

The deploy_pending marker this repo's skill-base.sh writes into a refused task's .return-meta.json (on postflight exit 6 from the completion-deploy gate) is never cleared by any writer once set -- confirmed absent from both reconcile-task-status.sh and update-task-status.sh. This is inert once a task reaches a terminal status (terminal tasks are never re-considered), but any future scan that iterates task numbers unconditionally (not filtered by terminal status) and reads this marker, such as orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint deploy_pending_any loop, risks stale positives if a task number is ever reused.
